DEL-04-05 keeps Anthropic provider access inside Chirality-owned runtime governance while adopting the Claude Agent SDK as the preferred engine substrate, protecting API keys, constraining network access, and keeping provider/SDK details behind adapter boundaries.

Preserve Chirality ownership: the SDK may host generic runtime mechanics but provider key handling, network policy, event semantics, redaction, and public APIs must remain Chirality-defined rather than SDK-shaped.
Treat keys as convenience state: API keys must not be written into the working root, document kit, runtime event payloads, logs, SDK transcripts if avoidable, or tool artifacts.
Key tests should prove positive behavior such as correct source precedence and negative behavior such as absence from project files and emitted records.
Fail closed: invalid base URLs, non-allowlisted renderer requests, policy violations, and provider failures should become typed failures preserving retry/debug context without exposing secrets.
Invalid base URL and policy-violation cases should stop execution before provider calls proceed.
Keep network scope narrow: current shipped network scope is loopback plus the Anthropic API path, and remote MCP, plugins, and non-Anthropic network tools are future-governed scope.
Redact at every boundary before details cross from provider/SDK internals into HarnessEvent, UIEvent, run logs, fixtures, or diagnostics.
A provider wrapper should be suspicious of SDK errors and stderr/debug text because upstream message shapes can drift.
Prefer a simple key resolver contract that returns { source, env } or equivalent safe metadata, never raw values in status objects.
Support both ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the documented order.
Use a URL parser rather than string prefix checks so credentials, scheme, host, and port are validated explicitly.
Renderer guard logging should capture safe policy metadata only, such as category and redacted URL classification, not headers or credentials.
Treat Node/SDK provider network calls as in-scope only when within Anthropic provider policy; the exact enforcement mechanism is TBD.
Normalize provider/SDK failures to typed application details without leaking upstream SDK object shape into public contracts.
Keep classification logic version-aware and covered by tests because SDK API and error shapes may change.
Do not allow ambient Claude settings to alter key, base URL, or network policy behavior in shipped builds.

A single provider wrapper centralizes redaction, key handoff, base URL validation, and provider error mapping but risks becoming too broad; keep it provider-boundary focused and delegate turn lifecycle to TurnEngine.
Separate helpers for key, URL, network, and error classification ease unit testing; prefer small helpers plus provider-boundary integration tests.
Do not rely on opaque SDK defaults for product-critical network/key behavior because it violates product-owned governance and may be version-sensitive.
Keep shipped base URL validation strict to Anthropic production API; test or dev-only escape hatches require explicit governance if introduced.
Log typed/redacted provider-error metadata and keep raw provider payloads out of durable records unless redaction is proven.
Key precedence example: a UI safeStorage key is used before ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; with no UI key, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is used before CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
Safe status example: API key status may report ui, env, or none and must not report the key.
Base URL example: https://api.anthropic.com with empty or 443 port and no credentials is accepted; non-Anthropic hosts, embedded credentials, or non-443 ports are rejected.
Network example: renderer outbound requests are restricted to loopback and the Anthropic API path, with broader remote MCP/plugin/network access deferred to future scope.
